content.comment_body: Hello, I'm trying to connect my [product_name] to my PC using Ethernet. Although the device is detected when I scan, when attempting to connect, I get an error stating, "The IP addresses of the PC and the target [product_name] are not in the same Subnet." I've verified that the IP addresses, gateway, and subnet mask match. Does anyone have suggestions? Thank you.

Hi, just press OK. [product_name] configuration software will automatically adjust your Ethernet settings as needed. When you close the program, your previous network settings should be restored. Hope this helps.

One more tip: If your PC typically uses DHCP, open your ethernet interface properties, select Internet Protocol V4, and then properties. You'll see DHCP enabled—switch to 'alternative configuration' and enter an IP address that allows you to connect to the [product_name]. Apply these changes. Disconnect and reconnect your network cable. The PC will try DHCP first but, since the [product_name] doesn't support DHCP, it will default to the alternative settings. You can also save the [product_name] IP address in your address book to avoid entering it repeatedly. Hope this helps.

Thanks for the quick reply. When prompted to add a new IP address, I click OK but then receive a message: "Failed to assign a new IP address to your PC." Also, my [product_name] is now stuck showing Setup, Network, and Diagnostics and does not return to the start page.
Hi [user_name], I followed all steps but the error persists. I've attached a screenshot of my settings. Thank you for your assistance.

Hello [user_name], can you provide the IP address and subnet mask for your PC? Are you connecting directly to the [product_name] or via a router? If using a router, please include its IP address and subnet mask as well.
PC's IPv4 is 192.168.1.74. Subnet mask: 255.255.255.0. Running Windows 7 Pro (not sure if that's relevant).

Make sure the first three segments of PC and [product_name] IP addresses are the same, and only the fourth segment differs. Both should have identical subnet masks. Your PC has 192.168.1.74, and the [product_name] has 192.168.0.1. This difference in the third segment prevents communication. If your [product_name] has a display, change its IP to 192.168.1.10 using the display. You don’t need to adjust the subnet mask.

Hi, ensure that you run [product_name] configuration software with admin rights and disable all other Ethernet connections except the one used for [product_name]. Ideally, connect directly with an Ethernet cable. I assume you are using the full version of the configuration software, not the demo.
Hello, thanks for your help. I followed your advice, but the issue remains. I’ve connected the [product_name] directly to my PC. It is detected, but still won't connect.
Please answer these questions: Did you install the configuration software with admin rights? Are you running it as admin? Is your PC's IP address fixed? What operating system are you using?
Thanks everyone, it’s working now. I had an issue with the configuration, and after fixing it, the connection succeeded. Appreciate your help!
Your screenshot shows that your [product_name] is on the correct network, and the status in the top right corner is YES, indicating everything is fine.

analysis.insight_summary: The user faced ongoing issues connecting their [product_name] to a PC via Ethernet, despite confirming network settings and trying direct cable connections. Automated IP configuration by the software failed, and error messages regarding subnets persisted, resulting in frustration. Recommendations from other users included manual network adjustments and running the software with admin rights, but only after further troubleshooting was the issue resolved. The product’s auto-configuration and error messaging were not effective in addressing the core connectivity challenge.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects a straightforward Ethernet connection between the [product_name] and PC, with clear network troubleshooting guidance or automatic adjustments by the software to resolve network/subnet problems.
